output.summary:
Found four implementation defects. Targeted isolated probes confirmed stale daemon configuration, missing provider health checks, and fixed smoke selection. Requested tests could not start because Zod is incompatible and the MCP SDK is missing; bun run check stopped because biome is unavailable.

Reviewed the diff and surrounding setup, daemon, provider, and smoke code. Found four defects. Focused fake-based reproductions confirmed the behavior. Standard targeted tests were blocked by missing/incompatible dependencies; a temporary dependency shim allowed 30 tests to pass, while two subprocess tests retained the dependency failure. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Apply config changes to an already healthy daemon
findings.detail: Init writes new providers and merge settings but skips service startup whenever the preflight daemon SHA matches. Factory loads its catalog and configuration at construction, so the running daemon continues using the previous settings. The isolated command `bun "$TMPDIR/setup-review.ts"` produced `healthy daemon config update: {"effects":["write","write"],"service":"already set","merge":"pr"}`, confirming configuration writes without a service update.
findings.suggestion: When effective configuration changes, safely reload or restart the daemon and wait for readiness before reporting success.
findings.failure_scenario: A daemon is healthy at the installed SHA. Re-running init adds a local provider or fills the missing merge policy. Init reports success, but the daemon cannot route to that provider and continues registering repositories with the old merge policy.

findings.title: Run smoke checks against the detected provider configuration
findings.detail: The production smoke adapter invokes a runner that imports the fixed PROVIDERS/MODELS catalogs and always schedules both native CLIs. It does not use the configured catalog or detected CLI availability. Newly detected local providers receive no live smoke check, while an absent CLI that doctor explicitly permits as a warning is still exercised. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/setup-review.ts"` with a zero smoke budget, preventing live calls, confirmed selection of both Claude and Codex plus the fixed backend list.
findings.suggestion: Pass the effective configured catalog and available CLI set into smoke selection, and exercise the local providers enabled by init.
findings.failure_scenario: Only Claude is installed and logged in. Doctor permits setup, but smoke attempts Codex and fails. Alternatively, init enables local-1234, yet its completion API is never exercised before setup reports success.

findings.title: Check providers that do not define a health URL
findings.detail: Provider diagnosis silently omits connectivity and authentication checks when healthUrl is absent. Supported presets such as OpenRouter and TypeSafe have no default healthUrl, so even invalid credentials receive only an 'API key present' success. The isolated command `bun "$TMPDIR/setup-review.ts"` with an invalid OpenRouter token returned only `[{"id":"provider:openrouter:key","status":"ok","message":"OPENROUTER_API_KEY present"}]`. This does not satisfy the requirement to check every configured provider's health.
findings.suggestion: Provide an appropriate read-only authenticated probe for each supported provider kind or report an explicit unresolved health check with a fix.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure `preset = "openrouter"` and set OPENROUTER_API_KEY to an expired or invalid token. Doctor reports the provider as successful without sending any request to OpenRouter.

findings.title: Implement the requested discreet-mode setup question
findings.detail: Discreet mode is unconditionally replaced with a 'not available yet (#37)' summary string. Init never asks the required question or persists a choice, including during interactive setup. The request does not exempt this step.
findings.suggestion: Implement discreet-mode selection and persistence with an explicit default for --yes, preserving an existing choice on subsequent runs.
findings.failure_scenario: A user runs interactive init on an empty configuration and wants discreet mode. Setup never offers the choice and finishes without configuring it.

findings.title: Apply new configuration to an already healthy daemon
findings.detail: Init writes newly detected providers and merge settings, but skips service installation whenever the preflight daemon SHA matches. Factory loads its configuration and provider catalog at startup and has no reload here, so the running daemon continues using the old settings. Focused command `bun --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-setup.ts"` produced `active daemon: {"added":["claude","codex","local-1234"],"merge":"pr","service":"already set","effects":["smoke","mcp"]}`.
findings.suggestion: When effective configuration changes, safely reload or restart the daemon and wait for it to become healthy before running smoke checks.
findings.failure_scenario: Run init against a healthy daemon with a partial config. Init adds a local provider and selects merge policy pr, but subsequent runs still use the daemon's previous provider catalog and merge policy.

findings.title: Run smoke checks against the effective provider catalog
findings.detail: The production adapter invokes the existing smoke main, which uses static PROVIDERS/MODELS and a hard-coded backend list. Newly detected or configured providers are never exercised. It also unconditionally exercises both native CLIs even though doctor permits one to be missing. A zero-budget check enumerated the actual smoke selection without making model or network calls: `bun --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-smoke.ts"` output `{"configured":["claude","codex","local-1234"],"smokeProviders":["claude","codex","omlx","twilight","openrouter","typesafe"],"localChecks":[]}`.
findings.suggestion: Build smoke checks from the effective configuration and detected CLI availability, preserving configured endpoints, credentials, and models.
findings.failure_scenario: A newly detected local server lists models but cannot perform inference. Init's smoke checks never call it and can report success. Conversely, a machine with only Claude passes preflight but fails the unconditional Codex smoke checks after configuration has been written.

findings.title: Check configured providers that lack an explicit health URL
findings.detail: Provider diagnosis only makes a health request when healthUrl exists. Supported presets such as OpenRouter have no healthUrl, so doctor reports only that their key is present and never checks whether the provider answers. Focused command `bun --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-setup.ts"` with an OpenRouter preset and invalid test token returned only `provider:openrouter:key` as ok; the recorded HTTP requests were exclusively `/api/health` and `/api/github/access`.
findings.suggestion: Supply suitable probes for supported presets and compatible provider kinds, or report an actionable diagnostic when provider health cannot be checked.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure the OpenRouter preset with an unavailable endpoint or unusable credentials. Doctor reports the configured provider key as present without attempting any provider health check.

findings.title: Implement the requested discreet-mode setup choice
findings.detail: Discreet mode is replaced with an unconditional 'not available yet' summary string. Init neither asks the required question nor persists a choice, including in noninteractive default handling. The focused setup reproduction recorded only local-provider, repository, merge-policy, and MCP questions, followed by `discreet: skipped: discreet mode: not available yet (#37)`.
findings.suggestion: Implement the discreet-mode choice and persistence required by the request, including defaults and preservation on reruns.
findings.failure_scenario: A user runs interactive init to enable discreet operation. No discreet-mode question appears, and setup completes without recording that preference.

The daemon loads configuration only at startup, so newly detected providers and the selected merge policy remain inactive. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-setup.ts"` produced `"effects":["smoke","mcp"]` while writing new providers and `"merge":"pr"`; no service action occurred.
findings.suggestion: When configuration changes, safely reload or restart the daemon and verify readiness before running smoke checks.
findings.failure_scenario: A healthy daemon started with no github.merge setting uses the auto default. Init writes merge=pr but leaves that daemon running; newly registered repositories can still receive auto merge policy.

findings.title: Run smoke checks against the effective configured providers
findings.detail: The production adapter calls scripts/smoke.ts main, which uses the static PROVIDERS and MODELS catalogs rather than the configuration init just wrote. It always schedules both native CLIs and fixed legacy backends, and never schedules newly detected local providers. The offline command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-setup.ts"`, using a zero smoke budget to avoid model calls, printed `"configuredLocalTested":false` and scheduled claude, codex, omlx, twilight, openrouter, and typesafe checks.
findings.suggestion: Build smoke checks from the effective configured catalog and detected usable CLIs, preserving configured endpoints, models, and credentials.
findings.failure_scenario: A machine with Claude installed and Codex absent passes preflight with a Codex warning, but init subsequently runs Codex smoke checks. A detected local-1234 provider is saved without receiving any live smoke check.

findings.title: Check requested repository access before persisting setup
findings.detail: Doctor runs before flags.repo or prompted repositories enter the configuration. Those repositories receive only syntax validation before being saved, so setup never checks their access or organization SSO authorization. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-setup.ts"` with private/no-access returned `"result":0,"repositoryReads":[]` and persisted that repository.
findings.suggestion: Probe access to newly requested repositories before writing configuration, applying the same SSO detection and fix text as doctor.
findings.failure_scenario: On an empty configuration, gh auth status succeeds but the token lacks access or SSO authorization for the repository passed through --repo. Init saves it and continues instead of stopping without partial configuration.

findings.title: Check connectivity for providers without an explicit health URL
findings.detail: Provider health is checked only when healthUrl exists. Supported presets such as openrouter have no healthUrl, so an arbitrary nonempty API key produces an ok key check without any provider request. The command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-setup.ts"` with preset=openrouter and invalid-key printed only `provider:openrouter:key` as ok; requests contained only daemon endpoints. This does not fulfill the required health check for every configured provider.
findings.suggestion: Provide an appropriate read-only health probe for supported presets and report an explicit diagnosis when provider health cannot be checked.
findings.failure_scenario: An explicitly configured OpenRouter provider has a revoked key or an unreachable endpoint. Doctor reports the credential as present and performs no request that could detect the failure.

findings.title: Do not treat a preset alias as the native provider
findings.detail: Candidate deduplication treats e.preset === id as evidence that the native provider is already configured, even when the entry has a different explicit id. Provider semantics allow an entry such as id="work-claude", preset="claude" with endpoint overrides. That entry does not represent the detected native claude provider, but init skips adding the requested native preset.
findings.suggestion: Compare effective provider IDs using e.id ?? e.preset, and independently compare endpoints for local-server duplicates.
findings.failure_scenario: Configuration contains a work-claude provider derived from the Claude preset and pointed at a compatible server. The native Claude CLI is logged in, but init does not add its claude preset because the aliased entry has preset="claude".

findings.title: Implement the requested discreet-mode setup choice
findings.detail: Init never asks about discreet mode or persists a choice. It unconditionally returns a string saying the feature is unavailable, and the new test explicitly expects that omission. The original request includes discreet mode among the setup questions and does not exclude it from scope.
findings.suggestion: Implement the discreet-mode setup setting with a default and preserve existing choices on reruns.
findings.failure_scenario: A user runs interactive init to enable a repository in discreet mode. There is no prompt or configuration path for selecting it, and --yes likewise cannot persist its default.

findings.title: Apply changed configuration to an already healthy daemon
findings.detail: Service installation depends only on the preflight SHA check. When init fills configuration gaps while the daemon is healthy, it never reloads or restarts that daemon. Factory loads its configuration and provider catalog at startup, so the new providers and merge default remain inactive. Reproduction: `bun --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-setup-probes.ts"` printed `healthy-daemon-new-config: {"added":["claude","codex","local-1234"],"effects":["smoke","mcp"],"service":"already set"}`.
findings.suggestion: Apply configuration changes through a supported reload or graceful restart, and verify health afterward. Preserve the no-restart behavior when configuration is unchanged.
findings.failure_scenario: A daemon is running at the installed SHA. Init detects a new local provider and writes it to config.toml, returns success, but the running daemon cannot route to that provider.

findings.title: Run setup smoke checks against the effective provider catalog
findings.detail: The production smoke adapter invokes scripts/smoke.ts main, which discards the configured catalog and constructs checks from static PROVIDERS and MODELS. Detected local providers are never exercised, overridden endpoints are ignored, and both native CLIs are tested even when preflight permits one to be absent. The isolated probe command `bun --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-setup-probes.ts"` enumerated smoke rows with a zero execution budget: config contained local-1234, but the output contained only claude, codex, omlx, twilight, openrouter and typesafe rows.
findings.suggestion: Construct smoke checks from the freshly loaded effective configuration and detected CLI availability, passing its endpoints, models and credentials through to the checks.
findings.failure_scenario: Init detects an OpenAI-compatible server on port 1234 and saves it successfully, but never tests an inference against it. A machine with only Claude installed also passes preflight and then runs Codex smoke checks.

findings.title: Check repository access for newly selected organizations
findings.detail: The access probe reads only the first repository in the old config. Repositories supplied through --repo or the interactive prompt receive no access check before being persisted; additional configured organizations are also ignored. The probe command `bun --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-setup-probes.ts"` printed `new-repository-access: {"repo":"private/restricted","ghCommands":["gh auth status"],"exit":0}`. With public/accessible followed by org/sso-blocked, it reported gh as ok and only called `gh api repos/public/accessible -i`.
findings.suggestion: Validate access to the selected repositories before writing configuration, including an SSO read for each configured organization that needs authorization.
findings.failure_scenario: A user has valid GitHub authentication but lacks SSO authorization for the organization passed to init --repo. Setup saves the repository and reports success without providing the required SSO fix.

findings.title: Collect and persist the requested discreet-mode choice
findings.detail: Discreet mode is replaced with a hardcoded skipped message. Init never asks about it or saves a default, despite this being an explicit setup requirement. Reproduction: `bun --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-discreet-probe.ts"` printed questions for provider enablement, repositories, merge policy and MCP, followed by `"discreet":"skipped: discreet mode: not available yet (#37)"`; no discreet setting was persisted.
findings.suggestion: Implement the discreet-mode setup question and persisted default, preserving an existing choice on subsequent runs.
findings.failure_scenario: An interactive user runs init for a repository that requires discreet operation and cannot select that behavior; --yes likewise records no discreet-mode default.

Found two reproducible defects in startup classification and signal detection. Targeted tests recorded 20 passes; other checks were blocked by Seatbelt restrictions and missing/incompatible dependencies. `bun run check` stopped because biome was unavailable. Effective OS isolation could not be exercised.

findings.title: Keep required Codex runtime state writable inside confinement
findings.detail: The outer profile permits writes only to scratch and, for editors, the checkout, but this environment leaves Codex state in the operator's CODEX_HOME or ~/.codex. Codex requires writable runtime state before starting a thread. An offline launch with a temporary CODEX_HOME set to mode 555 exited 1 with `Error: failed to initialize in-process app-server client: Permission denied (os error 13)`. Making that same directory writable allowed `thread.started` and `turn.started`. The command was `codex exec --json --skip-git-repo-check --ignore-user-config -c 'model_provider="offline"' -c 'model_providers.offline.name="offline"' -c 'model_providers.offline.base_url="file:///dev/null"' -c 'model_providers.offline.wire_api="responses"' -c 'model_providers.offline.requires_openai_auth=false' -c 'model_providers.offline.request_max_retries=0' -c 'model_providers.offline.stream_max_retries=0' -`, with `offline startup probe` on stdin. The file URL prevented a model request.
findings.suggestion: Provide an invocation-local writable Codex state directory inside scratch, preserving authentication safely and updating session/quota handling accordingly. Exercise actual offline CLI initialization rather than only the substitute.
findings.failure_scenario: On a host where confinement preflights succeed, a normal tool-enabled Codex invocation uses ~/.codex outside its permitted write roots and fails during initialization.

findings.title: Detect executable substitutions inside quoted strings and heredocs
findings.detail:
The detector treats quoted tokens and non-interpreter heredoc bodies as literal data, although shells execute command substitutions there. Targeted command `bun -e 'import { signalCommand } from "./src/harness/signals.ts"; console.log(signalCommand("echo "$(kill 123)"")); console.log(signalCommand("cat <<EOF
$(kill 123)
EOF"));'` printed `false
false`. Feeding these commands through either harness parser also emitted zero warnings. Consequently these signal attempts produce no run.warning feed item or report warning.
findings.suggestion: Scan executable shell substitutions in double-quoted strings and unquoted heredocs while preserving literal treatment for single quotes and quoted heredoc delimiters.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent submits `echo "$(kill 123)"` or an unquoted heredoc containing `$(kill 123)`; the shell attempts the signal but detection records no warning.

findings.title: Treating arbitrary agent output as a sandbox startup failure aborts valid runs
findings.detail: Every stdout line is scanned, including JSON containing assistant prose, tool arguments, and tool results. Merely reading or discussing `sandbox_init: Operation not permitted` sets broken permanently. Reproduced with `bun -e 'import { runSandboxed } from "./src/harness/sandbox.ts"; const line = JSON.stringify({type:"item.completed",item:{type:"agent_message",text:"The fixture contains sandbox_init: Operation not permitted"}}); try {await runSandboxed({cmd:["fake-cli"],cwd:process.cwd(),env:{}},{write:[],protect:[]},async opts => {opts.onStdoutLine?.(opts.cmd[4]); opts.onStdoutLine?.(line); return {exitCode:0,signal:null,timedOut:false,idleTimedOut:false,cancelled:false,stdout:line,stderr:"",truncated:false,durationMs:1};},undefined,{verify:async()=>{},nested:async()=>{},wrap:cmd=>cmd},true); console.log("success");} catch (error) {console.log(String(error)); process.exitCode=1;}'`. Output: `Error: Write confinement payload did not start (signal confinement also required): 0`.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish actual sandbox diagnostics from structured agent content; do not classify arbitrary JSON payload text as an operational startup failure.
findings.failure_scenario: A Codex invocation or Claude reader successfully reads a research document or fixture containing a sandbox failure diagnostic, then exits successfully. The wrapper throws ConfinementError and fails the run.

findings.title: Standard inline eval syntax silently bypasses signal warnings
findings.detail: The detector accepts only separate `--eval` and code tokens, missing the ordinary `--eval=CODE` form. Reproduction: `bun -e 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; import {signalCommand} from "./src/harness/signals.ts"; assert.equal(signalCommand("node --eval=\"process.kill(123)\""),true);'`. Output: `AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly equal: false !== true`. This prevents the required event-log, feed, and report warnings even though the tool input explicitly contains process.kill.
findings.suggestion: Recognize inline interpreter option values, including --eval= and --print=, and add parser-level regression coverage.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent calls Bash or shell with `node --eval="process.kill(123)"`. The invocation attempts a signal but produces no warning event or run.warning feed item.

findings.title: Restore every explicitly allowed inert-media extension
findings.detail: The regex excludes 18 requested extensions, including mp4 and pdf. The new tests also explicitly expect PDFs to block, contradicting the acceptance checks. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-media.ts"` with the repository's complete PDF fixture produced `plain.pdf isInertMedia= false` and a binary-content/block finding for plain.pdf.
findings.suggestion: Use the complete extension list from the request and restore tests requiring new and edited MP4 and PDF files to pass.

findings.title: Do not reject ordinary PNG metadata
findings.detail: The parser rejects valid standard chunks outside its narrow allowlist, including tEXt. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-media.ts"` after inserting a CRC-correct `Author\0Alice` tEXt chunk into the existing PNG fixture produced `annotated.png isInertMedia= false` and a binary-content/block finding, while the original PNG passed. This violates the requirement that inert PNG files pass without an allowance.
findings.suggestion: Keep the requested extension-based exemption instead of introducing an incomplete media parser.
findings.failure_scenario: A valid PNG exported with an ordinary author, description or copyright tEXt chunk is added or edited; the audit requires Allow: binary.

findings.title: Do not treat incidental sample bytes as embedded executables
findings.detail: Searching arbitrary media bytes for short signatures rejects harmless media. In particular, PAYLOADS contains the two-byte sequence MZ, which can naturally occur in PCM samples, pixels or compressed data. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-media.ts"` with a valid mono 16-bit PCM WAV containing one sample encoded as 4d 5a produced `sample.wav isInertMedia= false` and a binary-content/block finding; the same WAV with a zero sample passed.
findings.suggestion: Remove content-wide signature rejection from the inert-media exemption.
findings.failure_scenario: An ordinary WAV contains the valid PCM sample 0x5a4d, or another supported media file incidentally contains MZ; the audit incorrectly blocks the asset.

findings.detail: The request limits the change to 40 changed source lines plus tests. This new module alone adds 1,941 source lines, introducing decompression, checksum and codec implementations that the requested extension-list change does not require.
findings.suggestion: Remove the media-validation subsystem and implement the requested extension split and LFS correction within the stated budget.
findings.failure_scenario: Reviewing this patch against the explicit source budget shows that the new media module alone exceeds it by 1,901 lines.

Its audit output included {"rule":"binary-content","severity":"block","file":"document.pdf"}, and exited 1 with 'ASSERTION FAILED: inert PDF, PNG with Author metadata and PCM WAV should pass without Allow: binary; got 3 blocking findings'.
findings.suggestion: Use the complete requested extension list and restore acceptance tests requiring new and edited PDF and MP4 files to pass.

findings.detail: The PNG parser rejects standard ancillary chunks such as tEXt, iTXt and iCCP. A valid PNG containing only an Author tEXt chunk with value Alice loses its exemption. Command: bun -e 'import {INERT_MEDIA_PATH as p} from "./src/gates/audit.ts"; console.log(["mp4","pdf","bmp","avif","eot","glb"].map(e => [e,p.test(`asset.${e}`)]));' Output: [["mp4",false],["pdf",false],["bmp",false],["avif",false],["eot",false],["glb",false]].

findings.title: Do not reject legitimate media based on incidental bytes or metadata
findings.detail: The added parser imposes restrictions beyond the requested extension policy. It rejects ordinary metadata, such as PNG tEXt and GIF comments, and treats incidental signatures anywhere in audio samples as executable content. Reproduction: bun -e 'import f from "./test/fixtures/media/files.json"; import {isInertMedia as check} from "./src/gates/media.ts"; const b=Buffer.from(f["0.wav"],"base64"); console.log(check("tone.wav",b)); b.write("MZ",b.indexOf("data")+8); console.log(check("tone.wav",b));' Output: true followed by false. Changing two PCM sample bytes preserves a valid inert WAV but now causes a blocking finding.
findings.suggestion: Apply the requested inert-media extension exemption without the additional content parser. This also avoids the unnecessary 1,941-line module and restores the requested source-change budget.

This affects ordinary audio and high-resolution images.
findings.suggestion: Remove the size-dependent exemption restriction by using the requested path classification.

findings.title: Keep the implementation within the requested source budget

output.summary:
Found five reproducible regressions in classification. Targeted temporary-repository probes ran successfully. The existing test file could not load because installed Zod lacks prefault; bun run check could not run because Biome is missing. No checkout files were modified.

Confirmed four audit regressions with a standalone temporary-repository reproduction. No checkout files were modified. Targeted suite loading failed because installed Zod lacks prefault; bun run check stopped because Biome is unavailable.

findings.title: Restore every explicitly required inert-media extension
findings.detail: The exemption includes only PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and ICO. Required formats including fonts, audio, video, PDF and 3D models consequently block. The added tests explicitly expect several of these required formats to block, contradicting acceptance criteria. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-audit.ts"` with the supplied PDF and WOFF2 fixtures produced binary-content/block findings for asset.pdf and asset.woff2.
findings.suggestion: Implement the complete requested INERT_MEDIA_PATH list and restore acceptance tests requiring those media formats to pass without an allowance.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit a valid PDF or WOFF2 asset without Allow: binary; the audit blocks it.

findings.title: Do not classify readable text by embedded signature substrings
findings.detail: isForbiddenFormat scans entire text blobs for short signatures and ordinary words. Every occurrence of ASCII MZ or ustar causes otherwise readable source or documentation to be removed from the text set and blocked as binary. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-audit.ts"` produced binary-content/block findings for constants.ts containing `export const name = "MZ";` and readme.md containing `Use ustar archives.`.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the text-content classification for readable text; avoid treating arbitrary substring matches as evidence of an opaque binary format.
findings.failure_scenario: A source edit adds an MZ string constant, or documentation mentions ustar archives, without introducing any binary bytes.

findings.title: Keep executable text scripts eligible for normal review
findings.detail: modeRequiresAllowance is true for every changed file with mode 100755, regardless of content, and binaryPaths uses it unconditionally. This blocks ordinary executable shell scripts whose complete changes are visible in the diff. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-audit.ts"` produced a binary-content/block finding for build.sh containing only `#!/bin/sh\necho hello\n`.
findings.suggestion: Apply binary allowance requirements based on opaque content rather than executable permissions alone.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit a normal executable shell script, or change a text script's executable bit, without Allow: binary.

findings.title: Allow ordinary PNG metadata
findings.detail: The PNG parser rejects standard ancillary chunks such as tEXt, removing the exemption from otherwise valid inert images. Command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-audit.ts". A supplied valid PNG fixture augmented with a correctly checksummed tEXt chunk containing Author/Alice produced "metadata.png" in binaryPaths and a binary-content block.
findings.suggestion: Remove the unrequested restrictive parsing policy, or support standard benign media structures so ordinary PNG files satisfy the acceptance criterion.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit a valid PNG exported with author text metadata, without Allow: binary.

duplicates.title: Allow standard PNG metadata without a binary allowance
duplicates.detail: The PNG parser rejects valid standard chunks outside its narrow whitelist, including tEXt. Thus even a valid PNG containing harmless author metadata loses the requested exemption. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-audit.ts"` after inserting a CRC-correct tEXt chunk containing Author and Test into the supplied PNG produced a binary-content/block finding for metadata.png.
duplicates.suggestion: Preserve the requested PNG exemption for standard media variants instead of requiring this custom restricted encoding subset.
duplicates.failure_scenario: Add a valid PNG exported with an ordinary author or description tEXt chunk.

findings.title: Avoid output-limit failures when inspecting large text blobs
findings.detail: Classification now reads every apparent text blob through cat-file --batch, including a single blob larger than the 50,000,000-character subprocess limit. The batching condition does not bound that individual read. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-large.ts"` on a 50,050,000-byte text file with one added line printed `patch length: 159` followed by `Binary content inspection failed: ... cat-file --batch -Z ... exceeded 50000000 characters. Content could not be classified.` The block remains with both binary and gitattributes allowances.
findings.suggestion: Inspect large blobs through a bounded streaming mechanism rather than collecting their complete contents in the capped subprocess output.
findings.failure_scenario: Make a small, fully visible edit to an existing text file larger than 50 MB; classification fails and the audit cannot pass even with Allow: binary.

findings.title: Restore every requested inert-media extension
findings.detail: The exemption includes only five image families, omitting explicitly required fonts, audio, video, PDF, other images and 3D formats. Added tests even require fonts and PDF to block, contradicting acceptance criteria. Command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-audit.ts". Actual binaryPaths included "asset.pdf", "asset.wav", and "asset.woff2", with binary-content blocks for all three.
findings.suggestion: Use the complete extension list from the request and update tests to require those media additions and edits to pass without an allowance.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit a valid WOFF2 font, MP4 video, PDF document or other omitted inert-media format without Allow: binary.

findings.title: Do not classify ordinary text by embedded signature strings
findings.detail: Unanchored signature searches classify readable source and documentation as binary. Command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-audit.ts". Actual binaryPaths included "notes.md" containing 'The ustar format stores archives.' and "region.ts" containing 'export const timezone = "MZ";'. Both received binary-content blocks despite containing no binary bytes.
findings.suggestion: Preserve text classification for reviewable text; avoid treating arbitrary occurrences of short magic strings as evidence of opaque binary content.
findings.failure_scenario: A normal source edit adds an MZ string literal, or documentation mentions ustar or SQLite format 3.

findings.title: Do not require a binary allowance for readable executable scripts
findings.detail: Every changed file with mode 100755 is unconditionally added to binaryPaths, including fully reviewable text scripts. Mode-only changes also trigger this independently of content. Command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-audit.ts". Adding hello.sh containing '#!/bin/sh\nprintf hello\n' with mode 0755 produced a binary-content block.
findings.suggestion: Apply the allowance requirement to opaque binary content rather than executable permission bits.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit an ordinary executable shell, Python or JavaScript script, or change its executable bit.

Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-audit.ts"` after inserting a CRC-correct tEXt chunk containing Author and Test into the supplied PNG produced a binary-content/block finding for metadata.png.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the requested PNG exemption for standard media variants instead of requiring this custom restricted encoding subset.
findings.failure_scenario: Add a valid PNG exported with an ordinary author or description tEXt chunk.

findings.title: Avoid output-limit failures when inspecting large text blobs
findings.detail: Classification now reads every apparent text blob through cat-file --batch, including a single blob larger than the 50,000,000-character subprocess limit. The batching condition does not bound that individual read. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-large.ts"` on a 50,050,000-byte text file with one added line printed `patch length: 159` followed by `Binary content inspection failed: ... cat-file --batch -Z ... exceeded 50000000 characters. Content could not be classified.` The block remains with both binary and gitattributes allowances.
findings.suggestion: Inspect large blobs through a bounded streaming mechanism rather than collecting their complete contents in the capped subprocess output.
findings.failure_scenario: Make a small, fully visible edit to an existing text file larger than 50 MB; classification fails and the audit cannot pass even with Allow: binary.

new files blocked: README.md, asset.pdf, asset.wav, asset.woff2, code.ts, metadata.png, script.sh
edited files blocked: asset.pdf, asset.wav, asset.woff2, script.sh

Separate checks confirmed opaque additions/edits block, Allow: binary permits them, and a new LFS pointer produces no warning. The integration suite could not start because installed Zod lacks prefault; bun run check stopped because Biome is unavailable. No checkout files were modified.

Reviewed the diff and surrounding classification code. Targeted temporary-repository checks reproduced four regressions. Full checks were unavailable: Biome is missing and installed Zod lacks prefault/safeExtend. The focused reproduction stubbed only unrelated eval settings. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Restore all requested inert media extensions
findings.detail: INERT_MEDIA_PATH contains only png, jpeg, gif, webp and ico. Every other requested media format requires Allow: binary, directly contradicting the acceptance criteria. The reproduction command and output in the summary confirm that complete PDF, WOFF2 and WAV fixtures block on both additions and edits. Tests were changed to expect these incorrect blocks.
findings.suggestion: Use the complete extension list from the request and restore acceptance tests requiring those formats to pass.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit a valid PDF, WOFF2 font, MP4 video, WAV recording, or another omitted inert media format without Allow: binary.

findings.title: Do not classify visible text from incidental signature substrings
findings.detail: isForbiddenFormat scans the entire blob for short signatures and ordinary words. Consequently, fully reviewable ASCII text becomes binary: 'Custard is delicious.' contains 'ustar', and a TypeScript comment containing 'MZ' matches the DOS signature. The reproduction command in the summary reports binary-content blocks for README.md and code.ts despite neither containing binary bytes.
findings.suggestion: Preserve text classification for reviewable text; do not infer an opaque format from arbitrary substrings anywhere in its contents.
findings.failure_scenario: Add README.md containing 'Custard is delicious.' or code.ts containing 'export const x = 42; // MZ'. Both incorrectly require Allow: binary.

findings.title: Do not require a binary allowance for executable text scripts
findings.detail: Every changed file with mode 100755 enters binaryPaths unconditionally, including ordinary text scripts whose complete contents are visible in the diff. This expands the allowance requirement beyond binary content. The reproduction command in the summary shows script.sh blocked both when added and when its text is edited.
findings.suggestion: Determine whether content requires Allow: binary independently of the executable permission bit.
findings.failure_scenario: Add a chmod 755 shell script containing '#!/bin/sh\necho hello\n', or edit an existing executable shell script without changing its mode.

findings.title: Permit ordinary PNG metadata
findings.detail: The PNG parser rejects standard ancillary chunks such as tEXt, iTXt, zTXt and iCCP because they are absent from its fixed chunk whitelist. Thus even a retained media format fails the requirement that PNG additions and edits pass. The reproduction command in the summary inserts a correctly framed, CRC-valid tEXt comment into the existing valid PNG fixture; metadata.png receives a binary-content block.
findings.suggestion: Remove the unrequested restrictive media parser or ensure standards-compliant inert images retain their exemption.
findings.failure_scenario: Add a valid PNG containing a standard tEXt chunk with 'Comment\0A normal image comment', as commonly emitted by image tools.

findings.title: Restore all explicitly permitted inert media extensions
findings.detail: INERT_MEDIA_PATH permits only PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and ICO. All requested audio, video, font, PDF, 3D-model and several image extensions now require an allowance. The added tests even assert this contrary behavior. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-audit.ts"` returned binary-content/block findings for both `asset.woff2` and `asset.pdf`, using the supplied media fixtures.
findings.suggestion: Use the complete extension list specified in the request, and make the acceptance tests expect those media files to pass without an allowance.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit a valid WOFF2 font, MP4 video or PDF without Allow: binary; the audit blocks it despite the explicit acceptance criteria.

findings.title: Do not classify readable text by embedded magic strings
findings.detail: Searching anywhere for short signatures such as `MZ`, or ordinary strings such as `ustar`, classifies readable source as binary. This also removes it from the text sets used to prohibit hiding text with attributes. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-audit.ts"` reproduced a block for `example.ts` containing `export const signature = "MZ";`. After adding `example.ts -diff`, it printed `HIDDEN_SOURCE {"attributeMatches":{".gitattributes\u0000example.ts":[]},"textPaths":[],"findingsWithBinaryAllowance":[]}`: Allow: binary now permits hiding this text without Allow: gitattributes.
findings.suggestion: Preserve readable text classification and its attribute protections; do not treat arbitrary embedded signature substrings as proof of an opaque file format.
findings.failure_scenario: A request permits binary assets. A change adds readable TypeScript containing `MZ` and a matching -diff attribute; the attribute protection is bypassed without a gitattributes allowance.

findings.title: Allow ordinary PNG metadata
findings.detail: The PNG parser rejects every ancillary chunk outside its small whitelist, including standard tEXt, iTXt and iCCP chunks. This blocks valid inert PNGs produced by ordinary image tools. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-audit.ts"` inserted a correctly framed and CRC-checked tEXt chunk containing `Author\0Example` into the passing PNG fixture. Output included `{"file":"metadata.png","rule":"binary-content","severity":"block"}`, while the original `asset.png` passed.
findings.suggestion: Remove the unrequested parser restriction or support standard benign PNG metadata without requiring Allow: binary.
findings.failure_scenario: Add a valid PNG with an author field or embedded color profile; the audit blocks an explicitly permitted image.

findings.title: Keep executable text scripts outside the binary allowance rule
findings.detail: modeRequiresAllowance is true for every changed 100755 file, regardless of its content, and is applied unconditionally when collecting binaryPaths. Consequently, ordinary executable shell or Python scripts require Allow: binary even though their complete content is visible. Mode-only removal of an executable bit also blocks. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-audit.ts"` added a 0755 script containing `#!/bin/sh\necho hello\n`; output included `{"file":"script.sh","rule":"binary-content","severity":"block"}`.
findings.suggestion: Apply the binary rule based on opaque content rather than executable permission bits. Keep readable script edits and permission-only changes reviewable without a binary allowance.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit a normal executable text script, or chmod it from 0755 to 0644, without Allow: binary; the audit incorrectly blocks the change.

findings.title: Allow ordinary PNG metadata

findings.suggestion: Remove the unrequested parser restriction or support standard benign PNG metadata without requiring Allow: binary.
findings.failure_scenario: Add a valid PNG with an author field or embedded color profile; the audit blocks an explicitly permitted image.

findings.title: Keep executable text scripts outside the binary allowance rule

findings.suggestion: Apply the binary rule based on opaque content rather than executable permission bits. Keep readable script edits and permission-only changes reviewable without a binary allowance.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit a normal executable text script, or chmod it from 0755 to 0644, without Allow: binary; the audit incorrectly blocks the change.

findings.detail: The handler recognizes only WorktreeCleanError from the initial checkoutCommitted call. The unconditional discardChanges in the gates' finally block uses git clean -fdq without retry and throws an ordinary CommandError. That bypasses this handler even after a stuck implementer. Its exception can also replace an initial WorktreeCleanError, defeating the new recovery path.
findings.suggestion: Apply the retry and round-failure handling to the final cleanup too, and preserve an existing cleanup exception when finally also fails.
findings.failure_scenario: A stuck implementer's partial changes reach gates. Gates leave an untracked output directory and the final git clean -fdq fails once. The run fails immediately instead of retrying cleanup or proceeding to another implementation round.

findings.title: Final cleanup can bypass the new round-failure recovery
findings.detail: The gates callback always awaits discardChanges in finally. If the retried clean leaves nonignored files and discardChanges also fails, its ordinary CommandError replaces WorktreeCleanError. This catch rethrows it, failing the run instead of advancing the round. Isolated reproduction using the real Git helpers: `bun test "$TMPDIR/review-377.test.ts"` reported `cleanup error reaching round catch: CommandError Command failed (1): git clean -fdq` and `Expected constructor: WorktreeCleanError`.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the original cleanup error across finally, and apply the retry and round-failure policy to the final discard cleanup too.
findings.failure_scenario: A stuck implementer's clean fails twice while nonignored files remain; the finally block attempts git clean -fdq against those files and fails again. The run terminates rather than starting another implementation round.

findings.title: Process-group termination still leaves detached descendants alive
findings.detail: killTree only signals the invocation's original process group. A descendant that starts another session or detached process group survives, and the new wait returns immediately when the original group disappears. This preexisting limitation leaves the requested whole-process-tree fix incomplete. In `bun test "$TMPDIR/review-377.test.ts"`, a Python background writer calling os.setsid() survived runProcess returning: `expect(received).toThrow()` failed with `Received value: true` for process.kill(writerPid, 0).
findings.suggestion: Track invocation-owned descendants across process-group changes and terminate them before allowing invocation cleanup.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer launches a background writer through a tool that creates a separate session or detached process group. The invocation exits or is stopped, but the writer continues modifying the worktree during cleanup.

Found two confirmed shutdown defects using temporary subprocess tests. Both regression checks pass against the base implementation and fail against HEAD. Repository tests could not load because @simplewebauthn/server is missing; bun run check stopped because biome is missing. src/git/repos.ts contains no NUL bytes. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Children that clear their environment survive invocation cleanup
findings.detail: Session/group membership is considered only when environment data is hidden. A descendant with a readable, nonempty environment that omits the invocation markers is ignored, even in the invocation's process group. A standalone reproduction spawned a Bun background writer with env: {FOO: 'bar'}; runProcess returned successfully while it continued writing. Command: TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-mSgofg/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-mSgofg/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-mSgofg/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-mSgofg/claude-501/review-process.ts. Output: {"exitCode":0,"descendantAliveAfterReturn":true} followed by {"continuedWriting":true}. The Linux implementation likewise relies exclusively on environment markers.
findings.suggestion: Retain process-group and ancestry-based termination independently of environment markers, and confirm descendants have stopped before returning.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer starts a background command with a sanitized environment, such as through env -i or an explicit spawn environment, then exits or stalls. The writer survives and races worktree cleanup.

findings.title: Directory-based orphan detection selects unrelated processes
findings.detail: Birth time, orphan status, and a shared working directory do not establish invocation ownership. This fallback selects unrelated platform processes launched during the invocation, and stopMarkedProcesses then signals them. A standalone reproduction launched an unmarked orphan shell independently of the invocation and scanned with an unrelated marker. Command: TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-mSgofg/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-mSgofg/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-mSgofg/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-mSgofg/claude-501/review-orphan.ts. Output: {"unrelatedOrphanSelectedForTermination":true}.
findings.suggestion: Require proven invocation ownership through recorded ancestry, process-group/session membership, or an invocation marker; do not use directory and birth time alone to authorize signals.
findings.failure_scenario: While an invocation runs, another tool launches an orphan platform process in the same checkout directory. Invocation shutdown selects and kills that unrelated process.

findings.title: Directory and birth time do not prove process ownership
findings.detail: A newly orphaned platform process is classified as belonging to the invocation solely because it started later and shares its working directory. Shutdown consequently kills unrelated background jobs. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-process-boundaries.test.ts". Output: "invocation exit 0 unrelated orphan alive false", followed by "Expected: true; Received: false". The corresponding base-commit check passes.
findings.suggestion: Require evidence that the process descended from this invocation. Do not signal an otherwise unassociated process based on its directory and birth time.
findings.failure_scenario: While an invocation runs, another launcher starts a detached /bin/sleep in the same directory and exits. When the invocation finishes, shutdown kills that unrelated orphan.

findings.title: Preserve process-group membership when descendants replace their environment
findings.detail: Session/group membership is accepted only when the environment is hidden. A descendant with a visible explicit environment lacking the invocation markers is excluded, even when it remains in the invocation's process group. runProcess then returns successfully while the writer continues running. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-process-boundaries.test.ts" --test-name-pattern 'same-group'. Output: "invocation exit 0 same-group descendant alive true", followed by "Expected: false; Received: true". After allowing 100 ms for signal delivery, the same check passes against the base implementation.
findings.suggestion: Recognize proven process-group/session members regardless of environment visibility, and retain descendant tracking for processes that detach or replace their environment.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer spawns a background Bun writer with stdio ignored and env: {EXPLICIT_ENV: 'yes'}, then exits. The writer survives shutdown and keeps modifying files during worktree cleanup. A detached platform shell outside the recorded directory roots also survives while writing through absolute paths.

findings.detail: A hidden orphan is classified as an invocation member solely because it was born after invocation start and has a cwd under an invocation root. findings.title: Production scratch directories are absent from process discovery
findings.detail: Discovery reads scope.scratchDirs, but executeRun initializes that set empty and no production code adds directories to it. withScratch creates and removes invocation scratch without registering it. The binary-content flag was not reproduced: repos.ts contains no NUL bytes. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Detached descendants with replaced environments survive shutdown
findings.detail: Discovery starts only during shutdown. A descendant that starts a new session with a custom environment and becomes orphaned before inspection has neither a marker nor a proven ancestor. When its environment remains visible, the hidden-process fallback also excludes it. runProcess then reports successful shutdown while the descendant remains alive. Command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-p4xl5T/claude-501/review-process-tree.ts`. Output: `AssertionError: detached descendant must be gone before runProcess returns` followed by `true !== false`.
findings.suggestion: Track descendant ownership throughout the invocation or use an OS containment mechanism that survives environment replacement and reparenting. Do not confirm shutdown while owned descendants can escape discovery.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer spawns a detached background writer with env:{PATH:process.env.PATH,CUSTOM_ENV:'yes'}, then exits. The writer is orphaned before shutdown inspection and continues modifying files during cleanup.

findings.title: Working-directory matching kills unrelated orphan processes
findings.detail: A recent birth time, orphan status, and matching cwd do not establish invocation ownership. This fallback selects unrelated processes and sends them termination signals. A probe launched an independent orphaned /bin/sleep from the caller during another invocation; finishing that invocation killed the sleep. Command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-p4xl5T/claude-501/review-unrelated-process.ts`. Output: `AssertionError: unrelated orphan started by the caller must survive another invocation` followed by `false !== true`.
findings.suggestion: Require positive ownership evidence before signalling a process. Replace the cwd heuristic with recorded ancestry or OS containment.
findings.failure_scenario: Two activities share a working directory. While one invocation runs, the other starts an orphaned platform process with a hidden environment. The first invocation finishes and kills the second activity's process solely because its cwd and birth time match.

Found two reproducible shutdown defects on macOS. The binary-content flag is unsupported: repos.ts contains no NUL bytes. Targeted tests could not load because @simplewebauthn/server is missing; bun run check stopped because Biome is unavailable. Standalone process checks reproduced both findings. Repository files were unchanged.

findings.title: Directory overlap does not prove process ownership
findings.detail: A hidden orphan is classified as belonging to an invocation solely because it was born after invocation start and shares its directory. This kills unrelated processes without marker or ancestry evidence. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-process-probe.ts"`. Output: `{"result":0,"orphanPid":6791,"unrelatedOrphanAlive":false}`, followed by `ASSERTION FAILED: unrelated orphan must survive invocation cleanup`.
findings.suggestion: Require proven invocation membership before signalling a process. Track ancestry before reparenting or use an OS containment mechanism; do not infer ownership from cwd and birth time.
findings.failure_scenario: While runProcess is active, an independent launcher starts a detached /bin/sleep with an empty environment in the same directory and exits. Invocation cleanup kills that unrelated orphan.

findings.title: Detached descendants outside the captured directories still survive
findings.detail: The requested whole-process-tree guarantee remains unmet. A detached descendant with no visible marker, reparented before inspection and running outside the captured directories, is omitted; runProcess returns success while it remains alive. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-escaped-probe.ts"`. Output: `{"result":0,"descendantPid":9666,"descendantAlive":true}`, followed by `ASSERTION FAILED: detached descendant must be gone before runProcess returns`. The same probe against the base confirmed this is a pre-existing failure that the requested fix leaves unresolved.
findings.suggestion: Retain descendant ownership before parents exit, independently of environment and cwd, and cover detached descendants that change directory.
findings.failure_scenario: An invocation spawns a detached process with an empty environment and cwd outside the worktree, then exits. That descendant can continue writing into the worktree through absolute paths while cleanup proceeds.

findings.title: Working-directory matching kills unrelated orphan processes
findings.detail: A hidden orphan born during an invocation is treated as its descendant solely because its cwd is inside the invocation directory. This does not establish ancestry. I launched an independent process from the reviewer, orphaned it while an invocation was running, and observed shutdown kill it. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-377.ts" unrelated`. Output: `{"mode":"unrelated","exitCode":0,"alive":false}` followed by `error: unrelated orphan was killed`.
findings.suggestion: Require proven invocation ownership before signalling a process. Track ancestry while parents are alive rather than inferring ownership from cwd and birth time.
findings.failure_scenario: An unrelated launcher starts a detached, environment-hidden process in the same checkout during an invocation and exits. Invocation shutdown classifies that orphan as owned and kills it.

findings.title: Detached descendants can still survive confirmed shutdown
findings.detail: Discovery starts at termination, so a detached descendant whose parent has exited, whose environment lacks the marker, and whose cwd is outside the recorded roots is missed. runProcess returns successfully while it remains alive, leaving the requested whole-tree guarantee unmet. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-377.ts" leak`. Output: `{"mode":"leak","exitCode":0,"alive":true}` followed by `error: descendant survived confirmed shutdown`. The fixture spawned detached `/bin/sleep` with `env:{}` and cwd TMPDIR.
findings.suggestion: Track descendant identities before they detach or become reparented, so environment replacement and cwd changes cannot remove them from teardown.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer starts a detached writer with a replacement environment and temporary cwd, then exits. The writer uses absolute paths into the checkout and continues writing while cleanup runs.

Found two reproducible process-ownership defects. Targeted suites were blocked by missing/incompatible dependencies; bun run check was blocked by missing Biome. The binary-content flag was not reproduced: repos.ts contains no NUL bytes.

findings.title: Working directory and birth time do not prove process ownership

A separate, unmarked launcher reproduced this with `bun "$TMPDIR/review-orphan.ts"`: output was `{"invocationExit":0,"unrelatedControlPid":33510,"unrelatedControlAlive":false}`, followed by `ASSERTION FAILED: an invocation killed an orphan started by a separate launcher without invocation markers`.

findings.title: Children that replace their environment can escape shutdown
findings.detail: Linux discovery requires inherited environment markers and removes the previous process-group kill, so even ordinary same-group children with a replaced environment can survive. Darwin also misses detached descendants with a nonempty replacement environment once their parent exits. `bun "$TMPDIR/review-scrubbed.ts"` reproduced the Darwin case: `{"invocationExit":0,"writerPid":37518,"writerAliveAfterReturn":true}`, followed by `ASSERTION FAILED: detached descendant with a replaced environment outlived invocation`. Confirmed two process-ownership failures with standalone macOS probes. The clean-once retry probe passes. Targeted suites could not load because of incompatible Zod and missing @simplewebauthn/server; bun run check stops because biome is missing. The binary-content flag was not reproduced: repos.ts contains no unexpected control bytes.

findings.title: Require ownership evidence before killing an orphan
findings.detail: An empty-environment orphan is classified as belonging to this invocation solely because it was born after invocation start and its cwd is inside an invocation directory. An independent process can satisfy both conditions. I reproduced this with a sibling launcher creating an unrelated shell orphan in the same cwd: finishing runProcess killed that orphan. Command: TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-sjhTlZ/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-sjhTlZ/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-sjhTlZ/claude-501 bun test /private/tmp/lr-sjhTlZ/claude-501/review-boundary.test.ts. Output included '(fail) independent hidden orphan in same cwd must survive' and 'SystemError: kill() failed: ESRCH: No such process'.
findings.suggestion: Require captured ancestry, an invocation marker, or another proven ownership relationship. Do not treat cwd and birth time alone as permission to signal a process.
findings.failure_scenario: While invocation A is running, an independent launcher starts an empty-environment detached process in A's cwd and exits. A's shutdown discovers the orphan and kills it despite having no ownership relationship.

findings.title: Stop detached descendants with reduced environments
findings.detail: Detached descendants that replace their environment with a nonempty reduced environment lose the markers and session/group membership. After reparenting, they also miss the orphan fallback because hidden only includes processes with no visible environment. Shutdown then reports success while the writer remains alive. The same boundary-test command reported 'invocation exitCode: 0 writer alive: true', followed by '(fail) scrubbed detached orphan must stop before invocation returns' and 'Received function did not throw'. This leaves cleanup exposed to the original background-writer race.
findings.suggestion: Capture descendant ownership before detachment/reparenting or use an invocation containment mechanism that survives environment replacement. Add coverage for a detached writer with env containing only PATH.
findings.failure_scenario: An invocation spawns a detached background writer with env: { PATH: process.env.PATH } and stdio: 'ignore', waits until it writes, then exits. runProcess resolves successfully while the writer continues modifying the worktree.

findings.title: Working-directory overlap does not establish process ownership
findings.detail: The orphan fallback claims any hidden process born during the invocation whose cwd lies under its working directory. An unrelated invocation or user process can meet all these conditions and receive SIGTERM/SIGKILL. A standalone probe starts an independent orphan from the reviewer process while runProcess is active, using the same cwd and an empty environment. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-377.ts" ownership. Output includes `ownership: alive=false` and `AssertionError: unrelated orphan must survive` (`false !== true`).
findings.suggestion: Require proven invocation ownership before signalling a process. Track descendant identities while ancestry is observable, or use an OS containment mechanism; do not infer ownership from cwd and birth time alone.
findings.failure_scenario: Two concurrent operations share a checkout. One creates an orphan with an empty or hidden environment after the other starts. Finishing the other operation kills that unrelated orphan.

findings.title: Detached descendants with replacement environments survive shutdown
findings.detail: Discovery starts only during shutdown. A detached writer whose intermediate parent has exited has no observable ancestry or original session membership. If its replacement environment contains PATH but no invocation marker, it also bypasses the hidden-process fallback. runProcess then reports success while the writer remains alive. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-377.ts" descendant. Output includes `descendant: alive=true` and `AssertionError: invocation descendant must be stopped` (`true !== false`). The same probe fails against the base implementation, so this is an existing limitation left unresolved by the explicit whole-tree shutdown requirement.
findings.suggestion: Preserve ownership across detachment, reparenting, and environment replacement through descendant tracking or OS containment, and add a regression covering an exited intermediary.
findings.failure_scenario: The implementer launches an intermediary that starts a detached background writer with env={PATH: ...} and exits. The implementer subsequently ends. Shutdown returns successfully and cleanup begins while the writer continues modifying the checkout.

Reviewed the diff, confinement profiles, harness wiring, and tests. Found a timeout defect affecting longer verification commands. Targeted tests could not load the missing MCP dependency; bun run check stopped because biome was missing. Socket probing was blocked by this session's sandbox (EADDRINUSE). No files changed.

findings.title: Restrict loopback binding to ephemeral ports
findings.detail: The wildcard network-bind rule permits binding any loopback TCP port. Restrictions on network-inbound prevent listening on service ports, but binding alone reserves a port and can prevent other local processes from using it. This violates the requested ephemeral-only restriction. The new test combines bind and listen, so a denial at listen hides the successful prohibited bind.
findings.suggestion: Enforce the port restriction at bind time, or use the gate-results fallback if Seatbelt cannot safely express ephemeral allocation. Test bind separately from listen.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier command binds an available 127.0.0.1:12345 socket and keeps it open without calling listen. Another local process attempting to start a service on that address receives EADDRINUSE despite the port being outside the permitted ephemeral range.

findings.title: Disable the HTTP idle timeout for long-running reader commands
findings.detail: Bun.serve defaults to a 10-second idle timeout. This endpoint uses enableJsonResponse and awaits the entire command before sending its response, so even commands producing subprocess output send no HTTP traffic while running. Commands exceeding the HTTP idle window lose their connection; req.signal also participates in command cancellation. The configured command and MCP timeouts therefore cannot protect ordinary longer test runs.
findings.suggestion: Disable the server idle timeout (idleTimeout: 0), or explicitly manage it for command requests. Add an integration check that executes a command lasting beyond the default HTTP idle window and receives its successful result.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier invokes a local-server test suite taking 30 seconds with timeoutMs and idleTimeoutMs both set to 180000. The MCP connection times out before the command returns, preventing the verifier from receiving the test result.

Found two reproducible cases where incomplete gate coverage marks blocked criteria as met. Temporary regression checks both failed. Repository tests were blocked by incompatible installed Zod; bun run check stopped because biome is missing. No checkout files were modified.

Found a reproduced false verification pass and a restart recovery defect. Temporary regression tests produced two assertion failures. Repository checks were blocked by missing Biome, incompatible installed Zod, and missing solid-js/web; outbound confinement was not exercised.

findings.title: Require positive coverage for every explicitly requested file
findings.detail: The exact-command shortcut accepts matching file arguments without checking that each file ran. Bun treats these arguments as filters and exits successfully when one matches and another is missing. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/limitless-383-review.test.ts". The missing-file regression printed `gate exit: 0 ran: Ran 1 test across 1 file.` and failed with `Expected: "blocked", Received: "met"`.
findings.suggestion: Require every requested file to appear in passedFiles, including when gate and requested arguments match exactly.
findings.failure_scenario: Both the gate and criterion request `bun test ./present.test.ts ./missing.test.ts`. Only present.test.ts exists and passes. The verifier reports blocked, but the factory certifies both requested files.

findings.title: Do not substitute an entire criterion from one embedded command
findings.detail: The matcher extracts a Bun command and ignores additional verification steps around it. A passing test can therefore override a block caused by a separate operation that gates never exercised. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/limitless-383-review.test.ts". The separate-manual-probe regression failed with `Expected: "blocked", Received: "met"`. normalizeVerify subsequently permits the criterion to contribute to an overall pass.
findings.suggestion: Limit deterministic substitution to criteria whose complete verification procedure is the covered command, or preserve blocked status for additional uncovered steps.
findings.failure_scenario: how_to_verify contains `Run bun test test/server.test.ts` followed by a newline and a manual IPv6 service probe. Gates pass the existing IPv4 unit test; the IPv6 probe is blocked by sandbox permissions. The factory marks the whole criterion met without evidence for the IPv6 behavior.

findings.title: Partial command parsing can approve tests that never ran
findings.detail: The regex extracts only a command prefix and silently discards unsupported syntax or remaining instructions. For `bun test "test/loopback.test.ts"`, it extracts bare `bun test`, allowing any passing file to satisfy the criterion. It also ignores additional verification steps after a newline. Targeted command: `bun test "$TMPDIR/verifier-evidence-review.test.ts"`. Both cases failed with `Expected: "blocked"; Received: "met"` (0 pass, 2 fail).
findings.suggestion: Require complete, unambiguous parsing of the verification instructions. Preserve quoted arguments and refuse substitution when any requested test or additional verification step lacks coverage.
findings.failure_scenario: The criterion requests `bun test "test/loopback.test.ts"`, the verifier reports a sandbox block, and gate output contains only `test/unrelated.test.ts:\n(pass) unrelated`. The factory marks the criterion met despite never running the requested file.

findings.title: Interrupted gate completion permanently disables evidence on resume
findings.detail: RunContext.stage persists completedChecks and gateEvidence before marking the gate stage succeeded. A crash between those writes leaves cached successful checks referencing a running stage, which scheduler recovery marks cancelled. On resume, the gates cache bypasses execution, but this new status check rejects its evidence. Neither verification attempt repairs or reruns the gates, so an otherwise passing run ends as environment-blocked.
findings.suggestion: Invalidate and rerun cached gates when their evidence stage is incomplete, or persist gate completion and its resumable evidence atomically.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon stops after the gates checkpoint saves but before finishStage records success. It restarts on the same SHA, reuses cached gates, and both reader verification attempts encounter the loopback restriction. Successful gate evidence is rejected and the run becomes needs_human.

findings.detail:

nested/test/loopback.test.ts:
(pass) unrelated [0.03ms]

Found two defects, confirmed by three failing boundary tests. The 111 existing focused tests passed with a temporary Zod v4 shim. Unmodified tests could not start because installed Zod is v3; bun run check stopped because Biome is missing. Repository files were unchanged.

Found two correctness defects in gate-evidence handling. The 111 focused tests passed using the locally available Zod 4 module; default dependency resolution selects incompatible Zod 3. The full check could not run because biome is unavailable. No checkout files were modified.

findings.title: Exact command matching bypasses recorded test coverage
findings.detail: This branch accepts matching filename arguments without checking passedFiles, even when retained coverage explicitly shows a different file ran. Bun treats arguments without './' as substring filters: running `bun test test/loopback.test.ts` against a temporary fixture containing only test/loopback.test.ts.other.test.ts returned `1 pass, 0 fail`. The boundary check `bun test --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod-v4.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-gate-boundaries.test.ts"` then failed with `Expected: "blocked"; Received: "met"` for that gate result. The preload only substitutes the available Zod v4 export for the incompatible installed default.
findings.suggestion: Require retained passing-file coverage to include each requested file, including when command arguments match exactly. Do not let command equality override contradictory coverage.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate runs `bun test test/loopback.test.ts`, but only test/loopback.test.ts.other.test.ts exists and passes. Verification is blocked by sandbox restrictions. The engine marks the missing requested test's criterion met using the unrelated passing file.

findings.title: Gate-word filtering invalidates independently observed evidence
findings.detail: Any standalone occurrence of 'gate' triggers blocking, and a match in verify.notes blocks every met row. Thus independently observed application behavior such as 'the permission gate rejects the unauthenticated request with HTTP 403' loses its evidence and becomes blocked. Even the note 'Did not rerun gates.' invalidates unrelated rows containing successful targeted-test observations. Command `bun test --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod-v4.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-gate-boundaries.test.ts"` confirmed both cases: each failed with `Expected: "met"; Received: "blocked"` (overall: `0 pass, 3 fail`, including the separate coverage defect). This can recreate needs_human failures despite successful verification.
findings.suggestion: Detect actual reliance on factory results rather than keyword mentions, and avoid downgrading unrelated criteria based on global notes. Preserve independently observed evidence.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier successfully checks an authentication gate, or reports successful targeted tests while noting that it did not rerun gates. The criterion uses manual or prose verification instructions that cannot receive automatic gate substitution. Both verification attempts are downgraded to blocked and the run ends needs_human.

findings.title: Valid independent observations are downgraded to environment blocks
findings.detail: The sanitizer treats any standalone mention of gates as a factory citation, including words in independently observed passing-test output. It discards that evidence and changes met to blocked. Checking verify.notes also lets one incidental mention downgrade every met criterion. Targeted reproduction returned `expected met/pass; actual=blocked/fail` for independently observed evidence `bun test test/routing.test.ts: (pass) gates reject outbound connections; 1 pass, 0 fail`.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish actual claims of reliance on factory results from ordinary mentions of gates. Preserve independently observed evidence, and avoid applying a notes-level keyword match to every criterion.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier successfully runs a test whose name includes “gates”, or describes independently inspected gate behavior. Its criterion requires an inspection rather than a fully matching simple test command, so substitution cannot restore it. Verification retries and ultimately requests human intervention despite successful verification.

findings.title: Unchanged HEAD does not prove gates tested the committed tree
findings.detail: Gate setup and earlier checks can modify tracked source before tests execute. findings.title: Unrelated skipped tests prevent reuse of proven loopback coverage
findings.detail: passed() rejects an entire check containing any skipped file, and applyGateEvidence requires every check to pass that predicate.
