findings.suggestion: Evaluate skipped coverage against the requested files. Reject skipped requested tests without disqualifying independently proven coverage because unrelated tests were skipped.
findings.failure_scenario: The confined gate runs bun test successfully, records test/loopback.test.ts as passed and an unrelated platform-specific file as skipped. The reader cannot bind loopback, and verification still ends as needs_human.

findings.title: Ordinary mentions of gates invalidate independently observed evidence
findings.detail: gateClaim treats any standalone mention of gate/gates as a provenance claim, and including verify.notes in each row's check propagates that classification to every criterion. A legitimate note such as 'Validated the gate runner by direct inspection.' changes all met criteria to blocked, even when their evidence contains independent file references. Targeted command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-built/review-evidence.js"` returned `independent inspection: {"criteria":[{"id":"AC-1","status":"blocked","evidence":"src/harness/sandbox.ts:120 denies outbound connections.","publicSummary":"","requirement":null,"requirementCitation":""}],"overall":"pass","notes":""}`. Engine normalization then makes this a failed verification.
findings.suggestion: Restrict sanitization to actual claims of gate-derived verification. Avoid invalidating every criterion merely because a general note mentions the gate subsystem.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier independently confirms all criteria for a gate-related change and mentions the gate runner in its notes. Criteria requiring source inspection have no substitutable test command, so the engine blocks an otherwise valid verification.

findings.title: Unrelated skipped tests disable valid loopback evidence
findings.detail: A skip anywhere in the gate suite disqualifies every passing file, even when retained coverage proves the requested loopback file passed completely. This repository intentionally skips nested Seatbelt tests inside confined gates, so its normal suite cannot provide the intended fallback. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-gate-probe.ts". Output: "unrelated skipped file: blocked". The probe executes the unchanged pure evidence functions with Zod initialization excluded.
findings.suggestion: Evaluate skips against the requested coverage and covering checks, rather than rejecting evidence because unrelated tests were skipped.
findings.failure_scenario: The confined bun test gate passes test/loopback.test.ts and skips an unrelated platform or nested Seatbelt test. The verifier cannot bind loopback, reports blocked, and the engine rejects the passing file's evidence and ends needs_human.

findings.title: Gate keyword filtering discards independent verification
findings.detail: Any standalone mention of gates is treated as reliance on factory evidence, including independent observations about gate functionality or a note explicitly saying gates were not used. Because verify.notes is checked for every row, one such note downgrades all met criteria. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-gate-probe.ts". Output: "independent gate observation: blocked" and "unrelated note: blocked". The probe executes the unchanged pure evidence functions with Zod initialization excluded.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish factory-result citations from independent observations, and avoid using a global notes keyword match to invalidate every criterion.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier independently runs focused tests successfully and writes "The full gates were not used as evidence." in notes. All met rows become blocked; criteria requiring inspection or prose verification cannot be restored by command coverage, causing unnecessary retries and needs_human.

findings.title: Test-written output can forge authoritative coverage
findings.detail: The parser treats arbitrary test output as runner-owned file headers and passing rows. A real passing actual.test.ts printed `loopback.test.ts:\n(pass) fabricated loopback result`; loopback.test.ts did not exist. The engine nevertheless marked its blocked criterion met and attached factory provenance. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-gate-evidence.ts"`. Output: `{"mode":"spoof","gateOK":true,"coverage":{"passedFiles":["loopback.test.ts"],"skippedFiles":[],"summary":{"passed":1,"failed":0}},"status":"met"}`.

findings.failure_scenario: A candidate test prints a forged header and passing row for an unexecuted required test. When the verifier reports that required test blocked by its sandbox, applyGateEvidence converts it to met.

findings.title: Unrelated skipped tests disable the verification fix
findings.detail: Every gate must pass the global no-skips check before file-specific coverage is considered. Consequently, an unrelated platform-specific skip prevents substitution even when the requested file ran and passed completely. This repository deliberately skips Seatbelt tests inside confined gates, so its normal suite cannot supply this evidence. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-gate-evidence.ts"`. Output: `{"mode":"unrelated-skip","gateOK":true,"coverage":{"passedFiles":["loopback.test.ts"],"skippedFiles":["actual.test.ts"],"summary":{"passed":1,"failed":0}},"status":"blocked"}`.
findings.suggestion: For a targeted criterion, validate complete coverage of its requested files without rejecting unrelated, expected platform skips elsewhere in the suite.
findings.failure_scenario: The factory suite passes the required loopback test and skips an unrelated confinement test. The reader cannot bind loopback, so verification remains blocked and ultimately ends as needs_human despite the successful relevant gate result.

findings.title: Test-controlled output can forge factory coverage
findings.detail: The parser treats arbitrary stdout and stderr as authoritative runner records. I ran `bun run -` with a temporary empty target.test.ts and an unrelated passing test that printed `target.test.ts:\n(pass) fabricated coverage`. The real runner reported `1 pass` across two files; parsed coverage included target.test.ts, and applyGateEvidence returned `"status":"met"` for the empty target. Thus implementer-controlled diagnostics become engine-owned proof that an unexecuted test passed.
findings.suggestion: Obtain coverage through an independently validated runner channel that test diagnostics cannot impersonate, or refuse substitution when trustworthy execution coverage is unavailable.
findings.failure_scenario: An unrelated passing test prints a required file's header and a fabricated passing row. The required file contains no tests, but a sandbox-blocked verification criterion becomes met with factory provenance.

findings.title: Unrelated skipped tests disable substitution for passing targets
findings.detail: Requiring every check to pass without any skipped tests rejects a successfully executed target whenever another file contains an ordinary platform skip. This repository's full-suite gate includes Seatbelt tests deliberately skipped inside confined gates. An isolated `bun run -` check with a passing target and an unrelated skipped test returned `Factory gate substitution unavailable: candidate gate checks did not all pass cleanly without retries or skipped tests.` Consequently the default suite cannot supply the evidence intended to resolve the reported verification block.
findings.suggestion: Check completeness for the required target tests. Do not invalidate their coverage solely because unrelated platform-specific tests were skipped.
findings.failure_scenario: The full-suite gate passes the required loopback test and skips an unrelated Seatbelt test. The reader cannot bind loopback, substitution is refused, and verification still ends as needs_human.

findings.title: Recover gate evidence consistently with the cached stage checkpoint
findings.detail: RunContext.stage persists completedChecks and gateEvidence before marking the stage succeeded. A restart between those operations leaves a durable cached gate result whose stage is still running. On resume, the stage cache returns that result without rerunning gates or completing its stage record, while usableGates permanently rejects its evidence because the stage is not succeeded. A completed gate checkpoint therefore cannot support verification after this interruption.
findings.suggestion: Persist gate-stage success and its reusable checkpoint atomically, or invalidate and rerun cached gates when their referenced stage is incomplete.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon stops after the gates checkpoint save but before finishStage. The resumed run reuses cached checks, rejects their provenance, and sends an otherwise covered sandbox-blocked verification to needs_human.

Found three compatibility regressions in push isolation. All seven delivery tests passed; three landing tests that timed out passed individually with a longer timeout. Land-queue tests could not load because an installed SDK module was missing.

findings.title: Preserve credentials from trusted URL-conditional includes
findings.detail: Excluding remote configuration also disables trusted global includeIf.hasconfig:remote.*.url conditions. In a temporary repository with a matching origin URL, `git config --show-origin --get-all credential.helper` returned `trusted-helper` with exit 0. Running the same lookup through push-git.sh returned no output and exit 1. Thus existing global credential setup can disappear during delivery, contrary to the requirement that credentials keep working.
findings.suggestion: Preserve trusted conditional configuration using the factory-known destination without restoring untrusted repository settings, and add coverage for global hasconfig URL includes.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner's global config conditionally includes a credential helper for repositories whose origin matches a GitHub URL. Normal Git loads the helper; the isolated push has no remote URL configuration, skips the include, and cannot authenticate.

findings.title: Preserve the repository's reference storage format
findings.detail: The isolated directory preserves objects and file-based refs but omits reftable storage and extensions.refStorage. Reproduced in a repository initialized with `git init --ref-format=reftable`: a normal file-URL push of `HEAD:refs/heads/default-baseline` succeeded, while the equivalent push through this helper exited 1 with `error: src refspec HEAD does not match any`. pushBranch accepts HEAD by default, and the pipeline also explicitly passes HEAD on a delivery path.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the validated reference storage format and corresponding reference data, or resolve symbolic source revisions to the exact commit before entering isolation.
findings.failure_scenario: Delivery pushes HEAD from a reftable repository. The helper makes Git interpret its administration as file-based refs, so HEAD cannot resolve and delivery fails despite a valid source commit.

findings.title: Isolation drops trusted credentials selected by remote URL
findings.detail: Replacing the common config removes remote URLs used to evaluate trusted global includeIf.hasconfig:remote.*.url conditions. Credential helpers and SSH settings supplied by those includes consequently disappear. A local credential-fill probe succeeded normally, then failed through `bash scripts/push-git.sh "$probe" https://example.invalid/repo.git HEAD:refs/heads/test` with exit 128 and `could not read Username ... terminal prompts disabled`.
findings.suggestion: Preserve evaluation of trusted conditional includes using trusted remote metadata, while continuing to exclude repository-provided executable settings.
findings.failure_scenario: The global config conditionally includes a credential helper for repositories whose origin URL matches https://example.invalid/**. Ordinary authentication succeeds, but delivery or landing through the wrapper cannot authenticate.

findings.title: Forcing HTTPS breaks existing SSH-only landing credentials
findings.detail: The previous push used origin's configured transport. The replacement always uses HTTPS, so an installation whose origin uses SSH and whose trusted authentication consists of an SSH key or global core.sshCommand now needs separate HTTPS credentials. Preserving SSH settings in the wrapper does not help an HTTPS push. This violates the requirement to retain existing credential setup.
findings.suggestion: Obtain and pin the trusted destination, including its transport, before PR code executes, and use that explicit destination for the final push.
findings.failure_scenario: The landing checkout has an SSH origin, working SSH authentication, and no HTTPS credential helper. Landing previously succeeded; the new final push cannot authenticate.

findings.title: Reconstructed administration loses reftable references
findings.detail: The temporary common directory preserves only files-based refs and object-format metadata. It omits extensions.refStorage and reftable storage. A local repository initialized with `git init --ref-format=reftable` successfully pushed an explicit SHA through the wrapper, but the equivalent wrapper push using `HEAD:refs/heads/default` exited 1 with `error: src refspec HEAD does not match any`. Production delivery still passes HEAD in several paths.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the repository's validated reference storage format and required reference files, or resolve symbolic source revisions to pinned object IDs before isolation.
findings.failure_scenario: A factory cache/worktree uses reftable storage and delivery calls pushBranch with HEAD, or pushExistingBranch with its default source revision. The isolated push cannot resolve HEAD and delivery fails.

Confirmed command execution through both daemon push paths and a race bypassing the shell validation. The allowlist also rejects harmless local settings. Fourteen config cases passed with a longer timeout, but an isolated new case repeatedly exceeded the default timeout.

Found command-execution gaps in all three push paths, rejection of valid local config, and credential leakage in diagnostics. Local probes reproduced each issue without network access. The targeted test file had 18 five-second timeouts; six selected cases passed with a 30-second limit. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Protect the land queue and delivery pushes
findings.detail: Neither pushExistingBranch nor pushBranch receives the requested config isolation. Their worktreeGit wrapper still permits repository URL rewrites and protocol.ext.allow. Running `bun /private/tmp/lr-JcAFO3/claude-501/review-push-l54zsh30/probe.ts` against local bare remotes printed `FAIL: repository-configured command executed` for both delivery and land. Both remote SHAs matched the pinned SHA. These existing vulnerabilities remain unaddressed by the shell-only change.
findings.suggestion: Apply a shared push implementation that excludes repository config, preserves trusted global/system settings, and explicitly disables ext transport to both daemon paths.
findings.failure_scenario: The checkout config sets protocol.ext.allow=always and rewrites the trusted file URL to an ext helper that creates a marker before running the normal Git transport.

findings.title: Exclude repository config during push instead of checking it beforehand
findings.detail: The snapshot comparison does not constrain what the subsequent Git process reads. Unconfined check code can leave a background writer that adds receivepack, pushurl, or another command key after the comparison. The final push still names origin and has no protocol.ext.allow=never. A deterministic probe using the actual shell functions injected receivepack at push entry: `bash /private/tmp/lr-JcAFO3/claude-501/review-shell-2o0cvp0o/probe.sh` printed `FAIL: repository receivepack ran after successful config validation and snapshot comparison`; the remote still received the pinned SHA.
findings.suggestion: Make the push itself independent of repository config and use an explicit trusted URL, retaining the hardening and pinned refspec.
findings.failure_scenario: A process left running by bun run check changes repository config between the final snapshot read and Git loading config for the push.

findings.title: Do not reject ordinary repository configuration
findings.detail: The allowlist aborts landing for harmless existing settings such as user.name, user.email, and push.default. This introduces a broader precondition than the requested push isolation. With only a local identity added, `bash /private/tmp/lr-JcAFO3/claude-501/review-shell-2o0cvp0o/probe.sh benign` exited 1 with `Repository git config key user.name is not allowed; refusing to land`.
findings.suggestion: Ignore untrusted repository settings for the push without requiring users to remove unrelated local configuration.
findings.failure_scenario: A developer uses git config user.name to select a repository-specific identity, then runs land-pr.sh on an otherwise valid checkout.

findings.title: Give the expanded subprocess tests a sufficient timeout
findings.detail: The expanded cases retain Bun's five-second default despite their additional Git and wrapper subprocesses. An isolated rerun, `bun test test/land-pr.test.ts -t ': core.sshCommand$'`, failed with `this test timed out after 5000ms` and `0 pass, 1 fail`. The same case passed with a 30-second limit; all 14 config cases passed under that limit. The default file run had 13 timeouts, preventing a successful required check on this machine.
findings.suggestion: Reduce subprocess overhead or give these integration cases an explicit timeout consistent with the repository's other Git integration tests.
findings.failure_scenario: Run the new core.sshCommand case with the default test timeout on the shared macOS machine.

findings.title: Protect the delivery and land-queue pushes too
findings.detail: Only land-pr.sh changes. pushBranch and pushExistingBranch still use worktreeGit without excluding repository config or disabling protocol.ext. A repository-local url.<ext-command>.pushInsteadOf therefore executes a command even when the caller supplies a trusted explicit URL. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-push-probe.ts"` against both exported functions printed `delivery: repository command executed=true, pinned SHA received=true` and `land: repository command executed=true, pinned SHA received=true`.
findings.suggestion: Apply a shared push implementation that excludes repository config, retains trusted global/system configuration, disables ext transport, and preserves existing hardening and SHA pins.
findings.failure_scenario: PR code plants protocol.ext.allow=always and a pushInsteadOf rewrite from the trusted remote URL to an ext helper. Delivery or land-queue publication executes that helper.

findings.title: A config snapshot does not isolate the subsequent push
findings.detail: The final snapshot and comparison leave repository config active for the push. A process surviving the unconfined checks can change config after the snapshot, and safe_git then rereads it. A probe using the script's actual functions inserted core.sshCommand between comparison and push. `env -u GIT_SSH_COMMAND bash "$TMPDIR/review-land-probe.sh" 1 test .` printed `after snapshot: repository command EXECUTED` and `pinned SHA received: true`.
findings.suggestion: Exclude repository config during the push itself and use the trusted explicit URL with protocol.ext.allow=never. Do not rely on another pre-push comparison.
findings.failure_scenario: A background process started by PR checks waits until validation completes, then installs core.sshCommand or remote.origin.receivepack before git push reads config.

findings.title: Do not reject ordinary repository configuration
findings.detail: The allowlist aborts landing for harmless existing settings such as user.name, user.email, or remote.upstream.url. This changes the requested behavior from ignoring untrusted push configuration to refusing otherwise valid checkouts. The shell probe printed `Repository git config key user.name is not allowed; refusing to land` and `local identity: REJECTED`. The new tests also expect poisoned configurations to abort instead of demonstrating the required successful pinned-SHA push.
findings.suggestion: Ignore repository configuration for publication rather than banning it throughout the checkout. Test that planted command keys remain inert while the pinned SHA is successfully delivered.
findings.failure_scenario: An owner configures a repository-local commit identity, then runs land-pr.sh; it exits before installation or checks despite having a valid origin.

findings.title: Avoid printing credential-bearing config key names
findings.detail: Rejected key names are printed verbatim, but URL-scoped credential keys can contain passwords or tokens in their subsection. `bash "$TMPDIR/review-config-log.sh" 1 test .` printed `Repository git config key credential.https://user:sample-token@example.com.helper is not allowed; refusing to land`. Thus the new failure path exposes credentials through stderr.
findings.suggestion: Emit a generic diagnostic or redact credential-bearing subsection content before printing it.
findings.failure_scenario: Repository config contains credential.https://user:<token>@example.com.helper; validation copies the token into captured command output or logs.

findings.title: Protect the delivery and land-queue pushes too

findings.suggestion: Apply a shared push implementation that excludes repository config, retains trusted global/system configuration, disables ext transport, and preserves existing hardening and SHA pins.
findings.failure_scenario: PR code plants protocol.ext.allow=always and a pushInsteadOf rewrite from the trusted remote URL to an ext helper. Delivery or land-queue publication executes that helper.

findings.title: A config snapshot does not isolate the subsequent push
findings.detail: The final snapshot and comparison leave repository config active for the push. A process surviving the unconfined checks can change config after the snapshot, and safe_git then rereads it. A probe using the script's actual functions inserted core.sshCommand between comparison and push. `env -u GIT_SSH_COMMAND bash "$TMPDIR/review-land-probe.sh" 1 test .` printed `after snapshot: repository command EXECUTED` and `pinned SHA received: true`.
findings.suggestion: Exclude repository config during the push itself and use the trusted explicit URL with protocol.ext.allow=never. Do not rely on another pre-push comparison.
findings.failure_scenario: A background process started by PR checks waits until validation completes, then installs core.sshCommand or remote.origin.receivepack before git push reads config.

findings.title: Do not reject ordinary repository configuration
findings.detail: The allowlist aborts landing for harmless existing settings such as user.name, user.email, or remote.upstream.url. This changes the requested behavior from ignoring untrusted push configuration to refusing otherwise valid checkouts. The shell probe printed `Repository git config key user.name is not allowed; refusing to land` and `local identity: REJECTED`. The new tests also expect poisoned configurations to abort instead of demonstrating the required successful pinned-SHA push.
findings.suggestion: Ignore repository configuration for publication rather than banning it throughout the checkout. Test that planted command keys remain inert while the pinned SHA is successfully delivered.
findings.failure_scenario: An owner configures a repository-local commit identity, then runs land-pr.sh; it exits before installation or checks despite having a valid origin.

findings.title: Avoid printing credential-bearing config key names
findings.detail: Rejected key names are printed verbatim, but URL-scoped credential keys can contain passwords or tokens in their subsection. `bash "$TMPDIR/review-config-log.sh" 1 test .` printed `Repository git config key credential.https://user:sample-token@example.com.helper is not allowed; refusing to land`. Thus the new failure path exposes credentials through stderr.

findings.failure_scenario: Repository config contains credential.https://user:<token>@example.com.helper; validation copies the token into captured command output or logs.

findings.failure_scenario: PR code plants repository URL rewrites and protocol.ext.allow=always. A subsequent delivery or land-queue operation executes the configured transport command.

findings.title: Config snapshots leave the final push vulnerable to concurrent mutation
findings.detail: Validation and snapshot comparison do not isolate the push from repository config. A background process started by the unconfined checks can change config after config_after is captured. The final push still names origin and reads the changed config. Running `python3 "$TMPDIR/review-push-probes.py"` reproduced `post-snapshot config mutation: exit=0, markerExists=True, pinnedShaReceived=True` after planting remote.origin.receivepack between the final comparison and push.
findings.suggestion: Push to the trusted explicit URL with repository config excluded or neutralized for the push itself, including URL-scoped settings, and pass protocol.ext.allow=never.
findings.failure_scenario: A check starts a background writer that plants remote.origin.receivepack after the final config snapshot. The push executes that command even though validation passed and the pinned SHA remains correct.

findings.detail: The new validation rejects all local keys outside clone metadata, including harmless user.name and user.email settings used by the script's own commit step. Running `python3 "$TMPDIR/review-push-probes.py"` against an otherwise ordinary repository produced `local identity: exit=1`, followed by refusals for user.name and user.email. Previously valid landing checkouts now fail before installation or checks.
findings.suggestion: Isolate untrusted config for the push rather than rejecting unrelated repository settings throughout the landing workflow.
findings.failure_scenario: An owner configures their commit identity locally in a checkout, then runs land-pr.sh. The script refuses to land despite neither setting selecting a command or changing the push destination.

findings.title: Automated delivery and land pushes remain vulnerable
findings.detail: The change only protects the manual script. Both pushBranch and pushExistingBranch still consume repository-level command settings and URL rewrites through worktreeGit. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-push.ts"` with a repository-scoped insteadOf rewrite and protocol.ext.allow=always produced `delivery: repository-config command executed=true, exact SHA received=true` and `land: repository-config command executed=true, exact SHA received=true`. findings.failure_scenario: PR code plants a repository URL rewrite from the trusted remote URL to an ext transport script. Either automated push executes that script.

Found two detector correctness defects with failing direct checks. The harness tests could not load because installed Zod lacks .overwrite(). No files were modified.

findings.title: The sixth call is stopped before its changed result can arrive
findings.detail: observe() returns a loop reason immediately, and both harnesses immediately abort and latch stuckReason. A subsequent changed result cannot undo that decision. Exact failing command: bun -e 'import {LoopDetector} from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new LoopDetector(100); for(let i=1;i<=6;i++){const r=d.observe("shell","poll",`${i}`); d.observeResult(`${i}`,i<6?"waiting":"progress"); if(i===6){console.log(r); if(r) throw Error("progress was stopped");}}' Output: repeated the same shell call 6 times; error: progress was stopped (exit 1).
findings.suggestion: Resolve result-aware loop decisions before irreversibly aborting, while preserving counting for calls whose results never arrive and keeping the budget immediate. Add coverage where progress first appears on the threshold call.
findings.failure_scenario: Five identical polls return 'waiting'; the sixth identical poll returns 'progress'. Both harnesses stop at the sixth tool_call before processing its result.

findings.title: Late results overwrite the result of a newer identical call
findings.detail: The results map tracks completion order instead of call order. An older completion overwrites the newer call's hash, causing a subsequent unchanged result to be treated as progress and clearing valid occurrences. Exact failing command: bun -e 'import {LoopDetector} from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new LoopDetector(100); d.observe("shell","poll","1"); d.observe("shell","poll","2"); d.observeResult("2","B"); d.observeResult("1","A"); let r; for(let i=3;i<=8;i++){r=d.observe("shell","poll",`${i}`); d.observeResult(`${i}`,"B");} console.log(r); if(!r) throw Error("six unchanged results did not stop");' Output: null; error: six unchanged results did not stop (exit 1).
findings.suggestion: Track result hashes with call sequence numbers and reconcile out-of-order completions against the previous identical call, rather than the most recently completed call.
findings.failure_scenario: Identical calls 1 and 2 complete in reverse order with A and B respectively. Calls 3 through 8 all return B. Call 3 incorrectly resets the count because call 1's late A replaced call 2's B, so six unchanged calls do not trip detection.

findings.title: The threshold call is stopped before its changed result arrives
findings.detail: observe() returns the loop reason immediately, and both harnesses irreversibly abort before observeResult() can recognize progress. Direct reproduction: bun -e 'import {LoopDetector} from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new LoopDetector(100); for(let i=0;i<6;i++){const r=d.observe("shell","poll",String(i)); d.observeResult(String(i),i===5?"progress":"waiting"); if(i===5 && r) throw Error(r)}'. Output: error: repeated the same shell call 6 times.
findings.suggestion: Defer the result-dependent stop decision until the threshold call's result is classified, while explicitly preserving counting for missing results and the unchanged tool budget. Add coverage for progress arriving on the threshold call.
findings.failure_scenario: Five identical polling calls return 'waiting'; the sixth returns 'progress'. Both harnesses stop the agent on the sixth call before inspecting its changed output.

findings.title: Late results overwrite the baseline of newer identical calls
findings.detail: The results map records completion order rather than call order. An older result arriving late replaces the newer baseline, so the next unchanged result incorrectly clears the window as progress. Direct reproduction: bun -e 'import {LoopDetector} from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new LoopDetector(100); const c=(i:number)=>d.observe("shell","poll",String(i)); c(1); d.observeResult("1","A"); c(2); c(3); d.observeResult("3","B"); d.observeResult("2","A"); for(let i=4;i<=9;i++){const r=c(i); d.observeResult(String(i),"B"); if(i===9 && !r) throw Error("missed loop at call 9");}'. Output: error: missed loop at call 9.
findings.suggestion: Track result hashes with call sequence information and compare against the preceding identical call, preventing late completions from replacing newer baselines.
findings.failure_scenario: Calls 1 and 2 produce A, but call 2 finishes after call 3 produces B. Calls 4–9 all produce B. Call 4 is incorrectly treated as changed, so the six unchanged calls after call 3 fail to trip the detector.

Both parser paths correctly distinguish changing from identical results in direct checks. Found a regression in counting calls whose results never arrive. The harness test file could not load because the installed Zod lacks .overwrite().

findings.title: Preserve loop counting for calls whose results never arrive
findings.detail: Unresolved calls are skipped and block subsequent calls with the same key until finish(), rather than counting while still running as required. They can also be evicted before finish(), losing detection entirely. Targeted command: bun -e 'import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d = new LoopDetector(100); let reason = null; for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) reason = d.observe("shell", "poll", String(i)); console.log("six unresolved calls:", reason); if (reason !== "repeated the same shell call 6 times") throw new Error("six unresolved calls must retain the existing loop threshold");'. Output: 'six unresolved calls: null', followed by the assertion error. A second direct check confirmed that adding twelve unrelated calls makes finish() return null too.
findings.suggestion: Count unresolved calls toward the existing threshold and ensure missing results cannot erase a detected repetition through window eviction. Add coverage that checks stopping during the invocation, rather than only at finish().
findings.failure_scenario: An agent emits six identical calls with distinct IDs and no results. Both harnesses continue instead of stopping at six. If twelve unrelated calls follow, the repeated calls are evicted and the invocation can finish without any loop detection.

findings.title: Keep counting calls whose results never arrive
findings.detail: An unresolved call blocks counting every subsequent call with the same key until finish(), so six identical calls without results no longer stop a running agent. Moreover, eviction can erase the repetition before finish(), allowing the invocation to escape detection entirely. Reproduced with command: bun -e 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new LoopDetector(100);for(let i=0;i<6;i++) d.observe("shell","poll",String(i));for(let i=0;i<12;i++) d.observe("Read",{path:String(i)},"read-"+i);const actual=d.finish();console.log("finish after six missing results and twelve other calls:",actual);assert.equal(actual,"repeated the same shell call 6 times");'. Output: 'finish after six missing results and twelve other calls: null', followed by AssertionError: actual null, expected 'repeated the same shell call 6 times'.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the existing counting behavior for unresolved calls while allowing changed results to reset their key. Add regression coverage that checks detection during the invocation and ensures later eviction cannot erase a missing-result loop.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent issues six identical shell calls with distinct IDs and no results. It continues running instead of stopping; twelve subsequent unrelated calls evict those entries, and finish() returns null.

Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d = new LoopDetector(100); for (let i=0;i<5;i++) d.observe("Read", "file"); d.observe("shell", "poll", "a"); d.observeResult("a", "A"); d.observe("shell", "poll", "b"); d.observeResult("b", "B"); for (let i=0;i<5;i++) d.observe("other", i); assert.equal(d.observe("Read", "file"), "repeated the same Read call 6 times");'. Output: AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly equal: actual null, expected 'repeated the same Read call 6 times'.
findings.suggestion: Remove earlier occurrences of the progressing key from the retained window, preserving result matching and call-order handling. Add a regression covering another key near the window boundary.
findings.failure_scenario: Five identical Read calls, two poll calls producing A then B, five distinct calls, and a sixth identical Read call. The obsolete first poll remains in the window and causes the first Read to be evicted, so the detector misses the loop.

findings.title: Parallel test command disables factory gate evidence
findings.detail: gateTestCommand() rejects the new command's '=' and shell substitution, returning null for both this gate and the updated package test script. Consequently, passing candidate gates can no longer substitute for sandbox-blocked targeted tests. Probe: `bun -e 'import {gateTestCommand} from "./src/pipeline/gate-evidence.ts"; import p from "./package.json"; console.log(gateTestCommand("bun run test", p.scripts));'` outputs `null`. A direct applyGateEvidence probe retained the blocked criterion with 'candidate gate checks do not cover every required verification step.'
findings.suggestion: Support the narrowly validated parallel command in gate-evidence recognition and coverage checks, preserving rejection of arbitrary shell expressions.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier cannot run a loopback test in its sandbox, while the exact candidate's parallel factory suite passes that test. The criterion remains blocked instead of using the recorded gate evidence.

findings.title: Include the worker override in baseline cache identity
findings.detail: The new gate environment variable changes test execution but is excluded from gateEnvDigest(): it is neither a recognized variable nor a recognized prefix. Probe: `bun -e 'import {gateEnvDigest} from "./src/gates/cache.ts"; console.log(gateEnvDigest({LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS:"1"}) === gateEnvDigest({LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS:"8"}));'` outputs `true`. Changing the override therefore reuses baseline results from a different concurrency setting.
findings.suggestion: Add LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS to the baseline cache's recognized environment variables and test that different resolved counts produce different cache keys.
findings.failure_scenario: A baseline passes and is cached with one worker. The daemon subsequently runs with eight workers and reuses that baseline; an existing load-sensitive base failure is then incorrectly classified as a candidate regression.

findings.title: Supply the required measurements before selecting the default
findings.detail: The change selects four workers without supplying the requested serial-versus-parallel wall/user/system measurements, comparisons at 4/6/8 workers, post-split top ten file timings, or three failure-free parallel suite runs. Neither the submitted report nor the diff contains these results. These are explicit acceptance requirements for a performance change that increases contention on a shared machine.
findings.suggestion: Provide the requested benchmark results and three clean parallel runs, and use those measurements to justify or revise the fixed default.
findings.failure_scenario: Every full-suite entry point now uses four workers by default, despite no supplied evidence that this count achieves the requested performance and reliability or that the split files meet the approximately two-minute bound.

findings.title: Repository filtering silently fails against the previous daemon
findings.detail: The proxy relies entirely on the daemon honoring the new repo query parameter. The base-version daemon ignores it, so a newer CLI connected to the running previous release returns unrelated repositories and computes hasMore from those results. A read-only `bun run -` probe executing the new httpBackend against the extracted base GET handler returned [{"id":"new-other","repoSlug":"other/repo"},{"id":"older-requested","repoSlug":"wanted/repo"}] for repo=wanted/repo.
findings.suggestion: Provide a compatible filtering path for older daemons, or detect unsupported filtering and return an explicit error instead of silently returning incorrect results.
findings.failure_scenario: Run the new stdio MCP proxy against the base-version daemon and call limitless_list_runs with repo set while newer runs exist in another repository.

findings.title: Compact output still includes an unbounded dependency array
findings.detail: compactRun copies every dependsOn entry. Dependency counts have no input limit, so clipping title and error does not bound default output size. A read-only `bun run -` probe executing the extracted compactRun with 1,200 dependencies and short scalar fields printed `compact get_run size with 1200 dependencies: 30186`, exceeding both newly tested byte budgets before MCP envelope overhead.
findings.suggestion: Return a dependency count and bounded preview in compact mode, keeping the complete array available through full:true.
findings.failure_scenario: Inspect a run depending on 1,200 existing runs, or list several runs with large dependency arrays; default tool output again exceeds the intended compact byte budget.

findings.failure_scenario: A newer stdio MCP client connects to the previous running daemon and calls limitless_list_runs with repo set to target/repo while newer runs belong to other/repo.

findings.title: Compact output retains an unbounded dependency array
findings.detail: Both default inspection tools copy every dependency ID into their compact output. Dependency validation imposes no count limit, so valid fan-in runs still exceed the intended byte budgets. A focused check executing the actual compactRun function failed: `bun "$TMPDIR/mcp-review.ts" size` printed `compactRun bytes: 33185; expected < 4096`, followed by `AssertionError: false == true`. Five such runs also exceed the list test's 16 KB budget.
findings.suggestion: Bound dependency IDs in compact output and expose their total count and truncation indicator; retain the complete array through full:true.
findings.failure_scenario: A valid run depends on 1,000 existing runs. Default get_run returns over 33 KB before adding state and land information; a default list containing several such runs is substantially larger.

findings.detail: compactRun copies every dependency ID. findings.detail: The proxy delegates filtering entirely to the new HTTP repo parameter. The base daemon ignores that parameter, so a newer CLI connected to the previous release returns unrelated repositories. The tool then limits those results and computes hasMore as though filtering succeeded. Reproduction command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-7UZxPn/claude-501/mcp-version-skew.ts`. This executes the changed httpBackend against an injected fetcher implementing the base endpoint's behavior. Output: `{"requestedRepo":"target/repo","actual":[{"id":"new-other","repoSlug":"other/repo"},{"id":"old-target","repoSlug":"target/repo"}]}`, followed by `AssertionError: Repository-filtered list returned another repository against the previous daemon`.

findings.title: Compact responses still include an unbounded dependency array
findings.detail: compactRun copies every dependency ID. findings.suggestion: Bound dependency information in compact output, exposing a count and truncation indicator, and retain the complete array through full:true.

Output: "ΟΣ\nοσ", followed by 'error: Expected only the first line: ΟΣ' (exit 1). This contradicts the documented case-insensitive behavior.
findings.suggestion: Use Unicode case folding for ignore-case keys and add regression tests for Greek sigma variants.
findings.failure_scenario: Run dedupe --ignore-case with the two lines ΟΣ and οσ. Both survive despite differing only in case.
